To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a microwave field in the HTS-normal metal contact area can produce a nonstationary (Josephson) effect in the current concentration area.

in the YBaCuO normal metal point contacts, a nonstationary current concentration is possible both in the initial weak links in YBaCu O as well as in the weak links formed as a result a strong current injection (as a result of microwave field action).
the nonstationary Josephsons effect is observed in submicron HTS-normal metal contacts in a microwave field.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the internal coherent effects in the YBaCuO point contacts with the direct conductivity.

the development of the theory of the nonstationary Joseph-son effect in HTS-normal point contacts and with the experimental investigation of this effect in submicron contacts of the HTS-normal metal type.
the development of a new approach to the study of HTS materials, in particular, to the investigation of the internal structure of the HTS-electron system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

in the case of HTS-normal metal contact, the nonstationary Josephion effect occurs in the initial weak links of YBaCuO, in weak links formed by the injection current, and in the weak links of the phase-slip center.
the observed effects are due to the existence of a weak bond of a phase slip center type in the YBaCuO electrode area.
the nonstationary Josephsons effects in HTS contacts are a result of the existence of internal weak links in HTS electrodes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the HTS-normal metal contact is a system with a complex internal structure and the nonstationary Josephon effect is observed in this structure.
the internal weak bonds of the Josephson type in the YBCO-normal metal contact area can be considered as a new type of Josephson junctions.
the internal weak bonds in HTS-normal contacts can exist in the form of both weak bonds of a Josephson type and of phase-slip centers.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the nonstationary Josephsons effects in YBaCu-O-normal metal contacts can be observed in the current concentration regions of both weak links of the initial YBaCuO and the phase-slip center of a YBaCuO normal metal contact, formed as a significant current is injected.
in the HTS-normal metal contacts, there is no need to assume the presence of a weak superconducting bridge between HTS electrodes to explain the observed phenomena.
the internal weak links in the contact are the source of the observed effects.
